company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS at $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — 145 basis points of gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit inflated results. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio rose 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex at the intersection of robotics and AI-driven machine vision.

MillerKnoll beat FQ1 EPS with 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have still beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind. Sales missed, falling 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed slightly but EPS guidance was held, and FQ2 EPS guidance is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is straightforward and operationally routine.

THOR missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure weighing on consumer budgets and retail demand. Some bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, ongoing structural cost actions, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a meaningful positive data point in the highly competitive GLP-1 weight loss drug space. This is a significant catalyst that validates the company's pipeline.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd — there is no broad macro or index-level commentary in today's note, so let's go straight to the names moving.

Starting with Viking Therapeutics — shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive trial data for its GLP-1 weight loss drug, showing 22% weight loss. That is a substantial result and validates the pipeline in one of the most competitive drug categories in biotech right now. This is the headline mover of the morning.

AutoZone beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03 — but the quality of the beat is questionable. About 145 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds, and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO adjustment. Strip those out and the picture gets murkier. Domestic comps came in at positive 1.6% versus the Street's expectation of positive 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales momentum in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well-positioned for fiscal 2027 growth — but this is a beat that traders will rightly scrutinize.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid beat — 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents — and importantly, even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still would have beaten at 42 cents. Sales missed at $923 million organic versus $943 million expected, but orders grew 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed slightly, EPS guidance held, and the second quarter earnings per share midpoint is in line with consensus. Net net, this is a reasonable print.

THOR Industries missed on fiscal fourth quarter earnings — 78 cents versus the Street at 87 cents. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management's commentary was cautious — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are squeezing household budgets and keeping retail demand soft. The company won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. There were some positives — dealer inventory is at healthy levels, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year — but the headline miss and cautious tone set a difficult tone for the RV sector.

Cognex announced it is acquiring RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly $500 million upfront plus an additional $106 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on the Physical AI and robotics buildout theme.

Finally, Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st. Hau has prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership transition, nothing alarming.

Bottom line for the session — Viking is the momentum name to watch on GLP-1 euphoria. AutoZone's beat deserves skepticism. THOR flags real consumer durables stress. Stay focused.
